correctness.rationale: Example 11 and Example 19 of arXiv:2609.28354v1 give the two exact formulas used. Their simultaneous zero set is determined by the classical fact that \(\zeta(-n)=0\) exactly for positive even \(n\). The reverse implication for these two limits uses Theorem 1 only for the regular value, plus the explicit product formula for the \((23)\) value. Common vanishing of all six then implies vanishing of these two, establishing only the necessary direction claimed.

evidence: Conjecture 2 is broader but conjectural. Theorem 1 proves forward vanishing only for three distinguished types of ordered limit under the trivial-zero condition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader conjecture does not cover a proved necessary direction on a full infinite slice. The source does not derive the two-limit detector or the slice-wise only-if implication.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Combining those ingredients with the exact negative-integer zero set of the Riemann zeta function yields a new necessary-direction result. The source does not draw that implication.

evidence: The claim was compared in the equivalent form: on the slice \(\ell_{12}=0\), simultaneous vanishing of the regular and \((23)\)-ordered limits is equivalent to positive diagonal exponents of odd total weight; hence common vanishing of all six implies that condition.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The two-limit equivalence is proved directly. The all-six statement used is only the implication from common vanishing to vanishing of the selected two; no unproved sufficiency for all six is assumed.

value.rationale: The off-diagonal-zero slice is a natural decoupling boundary of the \(\mathrm A_2\) root-system zeta function. The result proves the converse/necessary half of a newly stated all-orders conjecture on this entire infinite slice and shows that two specific orderings detect the condition, isolating where genuinely coupled behavior must begin.
